title: Compact surface balance, scroll affordance & density regressions across Safari/Firefox/mobile - QA & bug triage
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Scope: Investigate a cluster of visual and interaction regressions surfaced in the compact/dense mode of the UI kit when rendered in Safari (macOS + iOS) and Firefox. Affects tokens (spacing and surface elevation), table row clipping during scroll-snap/virtualization, chart legend wrap/overflow, and button hit-area on small screens. Goal is to triage, create engineering tickets for fixes, and land temporary design workarounds that preserve accessibility and visual consistency until runtime fixes are available.
updates: 2026-03-10 - Ava M.: Initial exploratory pass. Reproduced three classes of issues on device lab (iPhone 13 iOS 16.4 Safari, MacBook Pro macOS 12.6 Safari 16, and Windows VM Firefox 122): 1) compact-token vertical collapse under 320px causing icon/button overlap; 2) table sticky header overlap with compact row when momentum scroll + overscroll bounce on iOS; 3) chart legend line-wrapping differs between browsers causing clipping in compact density.

2026-03-11 - Liam O.: Added reproducible steps and attached screenshots to Confluence. Prioritized defects by customer impact: table/sticky header and button hit-area are P0 for support-facing flows, chart legend is P1. Linked prototype and short-term CSS mitigations for table z-index and pointer-events.

2026-03-12 - Design review: Collective decision to avoid increasing touch targets beyond current token size for compact mode; instead we'll implement an explicit 'compact-tap' affordance: swapping inline icon-only buttons for a small overflow menu on mobile. Engineering requested acceptance criteria and visual tokens for 3 density breakpoints.

2026-03-13 - Eng sync: Internal engineering spike (ENG-20492) authorized to validate virtualization + sticky header interplay. Eng requests a separate small repro harness for continuous integration (minimal DOM + virtualization flags). UX to deliver token spacing deltas and chart legend truncation rules.

2026-03-14 - QA pass: Confirmed that applying -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch did not resolve header overlap; temporary CSS workaround using contain: paint and will-change helped render but introduced subpixel blurring on Safari. Documented as unacceptable; engineering to explore layout/paint boundary fixes instead of hacky containment.
2026-03-14 - Next: Create ENG tickets described below and attach design handoff (Figma frames + CSS tokens).
reproductions: Table sticky header overlap (iOS Safari): 1) Open Dashboard > Table view in compact mode on iPhone 13 Safari; 2) Fast scroll a long list to trigger momentum + release; 3) Observe header visually overlapping rows when virtualization mounts new rows. Expected: header remains above content without visual clipping.

Compact token icon overlap (Firefox): 1) Resize browser width to 320px, switch to compact token set in UI Kit demo; 2) Inspect token with icon + label; 3) See icon overlapping label baseline and touch target reduced. Expected: consistent spacing and preserved 44px minimum touch target when not in forced-compact UX.

Chart legend clipping (macOS Safari): 1) Open Reports > Chart with legend set to side+wrap in compact density; 2) Reduce container width to narrow breakpoint; 3) Legend wraps and last line is clipped behind container mask. Expected: legend truncates with ellipsis or moves into overflow menu.

Button hit-area on Android Chrome (hybrid): reproduce by toggling compact density and using external keyboard focus; focus ring appears offset due to transform rounding differences. Expected: focus ring centered on element and meets 3:1 contrast on accessible focus color.
Edgecase: backdrop-filter / blur differences: show modal with translucent surface in Safari vs Firefox and note different blur radii causing perceived depth shift in compact surfaces.
decisions: Do not increase base compact token size to meet touch guidelines; instead implement micro-affordances (overflow menu or explicit tappable area) for dense lists on mobile.
Avoid -webkit-overflow-scrolling or contain:paint as long-term fixes due to rendering artifacts; prefer layout/paint boundary changes in runtime and virtualization logic in the serving layer.
For chart legends, prefer deterministic truncation rules (single-line ellipsis with overflow menu) rather than relying on browser wrapping behavior which diverges between engines.
All changes must include accessibility acceptance criteria (focus, contrast, minimum hit area or explicit affordance).
next_steps: Create ENG tickets: ENG-20492 (virtualization + sticky header repro + fix), ENG-20513 (token spacing deltas + CSS token shim), ENG-20514 (chart legend truncation component + overflow menu).
Design: Deliver Figma frames for three density breakpoints and annotated CSS token values (spacing, line-height, hit-area) by 2026-03-18.
QA: Add automated visual regressions for compact mode on BrowserStack iOS Safari and Firefox 122 (screenshots + pixel-diff thresholds) - target by 2026-03-21.
Create minimal repro harness repo and link to PR template so eng can iterate quickly. Attach to ENG-20492.
Customer comms: Draft short internal note for Support + Solutions documenting the temporary mitigations and ETA for fixes.
